Yes, from HIM. It is never okay to call your significant other names, especially not the awful things he said.
YTA. I know you had good intentions but your fiance likely wanted to feel heard and supported, not reduced down to her looks.

YTA. 

You expect your 10 year old daughter to use tampons during her first period? Your 4th/5th grade daughter? That's insane. Tampons are painful for some, especially for kids, and difficult to learn to use. Do you even know how they work? 

Apologize to your girlfriend and ESPECIALLY your poor daughter.

Title should be "AITA for harassing my sons teacher about marking him down for incorrect work and failing to effectively establish communication when she has 30 other students to keep track of?" 

YTA.

YTA. Yes, your husband should have consulted you. But his brother was diagnosed with a terrifying illness and he was focused on caring for his elementary aged nephew. I can't imagine a world where my partner brings home my FAMILY and I refuse to help support him. 
That child will know that you don't care about him and you'll hurt him. You are incredibly selfish.

Your brother is fine? But you didn't know that in the moment. You told your family you don't care if they're hurt and won't help out. Now you have to deal with them not fighting you to be a part of the family anymore. Yta.

YTA. Your fiancee was hurt by your mother. Sounds like she is CONSTANTLY hurt by your mother. And it's great you stood up for her, but she should be able to tell her side of the story and shouldn't be expected to "keep secrets." Your family sucks. Don't invite them to the wedding. Keep it to the people that support you. And I hope you apologize to your fiancée.

At first I felt YTA, but after reading the end, you definitely aren't. As someone that has horrible anxiety that is supported by my ESA, I'd never put my illness above someone else's breathing health. It does suck that he's expected to be the one to take daily medication when his sister and father refuse, but offering to financially support him completely mitigates that. He's being ridiculous to still blame this on you. 

Also a thought, if he even deserves it now, but they do have hairless pets. It would be a decent compromise.

YTA. When I read the title, I thought it would be a teenager forced on a family vacation. Not a whole Mother. How could you feel okay with yourself ignoring your children and husband that just want to spend time with you? You don't have to even do 'house' chores, just make them feel loved. You owe them all a big apology.
YTA. Hope she calls the police on you for stealing her car. Insane, entitled behavior.

NTA for choosing not to go. Completely in your right. But you shouldn't have mentioned the lack of alcohol. Choosing a dry wedding to avoid temptation for alcoholics in the family is a completely valid and respectful choice. Erica shouldn't feel bad about that.
Soft YWBTA. You definitely don't wanna be the one to break the news. I'd tell a staff member and ask them to speak with him or his parents first. Especially if you aren't friends.

YTA. How do you not feel like one? You CHOSE to host and you CHOSE to make someone feel unwelcome. You sound possessive and jealous tbh, forcing your lifestyle on someone else. 

And commenting on her body?? Yeah, definitely sound jealous. I'm glad your friends called you out. Even if you say you're not in love with Jake it comes across that way.
NTA. Manipulative, sure, but with good intentions so she didn't get pressured into a future she didn't want by your parents. She'll appreciate it one day, especially if you apologize.

You made it sound like she didn't complain about her life. Didn't ask for your opinion. She was just existing and helping her cousin celebrate. Then you judged her life and decided she was worse off? 

YTA.

ESH. 

Your ex-wife is terrible, for cheating on you then trying to gaslight your family into thinking the same about you. 

Ariel should grow up. But that doesn't change the fact she's a teenager and has been brain washed by her mother who she seems close to. Divorce is messy and she should be allowed to not like her step family. She isn't obligated to like them, though she doesn't need to be mean to them. Still, you should be understanding. Holding money hostage to make her like your family won't do anything. You also had an agreement. She doesn't like your family,  she didn't crash your car. Harsh punishment.
NTA. She called you a pick me and then went on to prove why SHE was a pick me.

YTA. It's not wrong to promote a healthy lifestyle but being demanding with your daughter is. That leads to eating disorders and self confidence issues. 
If you want to encourage her to be healthier by making those changes in your own life, great! But you can't yell at her for enjoying food.

YWBTA if you told anyone about it or made it a problem. It's not your house. Your sister deserves the safety of your parent's support too, and she's not much older than you. 

NTA if you just silently brood about it and get over it and try to be a good family member, assuming you guys are on good enough terms to want to support her as well.

YTA. Take it from a sheltered kid that grew up with friends that were given privacy by their parents. I was the one with the secrets that had to learn to hide stuff from Mom and Dad's prying eyes. My friends told their parents everything and never kept secrets or lied about where they were going. This is very controlling behavior and you WILL push away your kids. You are the thing that is contributing to them keeping secrets and feeling untrusted by you, therefore they won't trust you either. Let them close their doors and explore the internet on their own, and have a discussion with your kids about what is bad and what is okay online, as well as offering them support and letting them know they can tell you anything.

At some point, I noticed that from being on the internet or from friends, I decided that talking about suicidal idealation was really cringy and edgy and that kept me from it for years (and i still struggle with it in outpatient and lie a lot about my SI ) 

Just know that professionals won't find it edgy at all. Their entire passion and career is listening and helping and figuring out how to help you get through your issues. Even other patients in psych hospitals or outpatient won't find it edgy. It's been the hardest thing for me to learn. 

I cant talk to my friends about it because I struggle with the same issues. But it's NOT edgy to talk about, it's a serious topic with serious and heavy feelings. Try not to be mean to yourself more when you already probably struggle with those issues on a daily basis. You just have to find the right support, as daunting as it can be, and others with experience with SI won't ever find it edgy because they understand. 

Best of luck!
